label: Orange & Green
_shapeNote: UNUSUAL SHAPE — READ BEFORE WIRING THIS UP. (1) `enemy` is deliberately the CONTROLLER, not a monster. obj_orange_enemy and obj_green_enemy are the two visible obj_monsterparent enemies (objects.tsv:404 / :150; encounter 221, monstertypes 113/114) but neither holds a single attack dispatch. obj_orange_enemy_Create_0.gml:32 does `instance_create(x, y, obj_orange_green_controller);` and that controller owns the box, the turn lengths, the dispatcher, the powerup ladder, the finale and the healing-egg turn. obj_orange_enemy_CleanUp_0.gml destroys it again. Every slice below must be replayed with self = an obj_orange_green_controller instance, because they read its instance variables (powerup, healing_egg_con, endcon, condescendending, admireending, endtimer, rtimer). (2) There is NO `monsterattackname` ANYWHERE in this fight — `grep -n monsterattackname` over all obj_orange_enemy_*, obj_green_enemy_* and obj_orange_green_controller_* files returns nothing (exit 1). gen_attacks.js's announcement scan therefore finds ZERO attacks no matter what goes in `enemy`; this roster is DECLARED, not scanned, and `extraAttackFiles` is deliberately omitted (it would only add a '0 attacks announced' note). (3) selectorScan does NOT apply. This is not a Ch1-style numeric ladder. The per-turn chooser is a BOOLEAN on another object's variable — `if (i_ex(obj_orange_enemy) && obj_orange_enemy.uppercut_life < 1) {314} else {131}` — and the finale chooser branches on two booleans on self, `condescendending` / `admireending`. (4) obj_orangeheart_enemy from the starting leads is NOT part of this fight — see `exclusions`.

boxBlock._verified: Step_0:514-538, 1005 chars, brace-balanced, anchor occurs exactly once (verified by replaying gen_attacks.js strip()+ifStatementEnd() against the file). No endAnchor needed.
boxBlock._note: Creates obj_growtangle at (viewX+320, viewY+170) and then forces `maxxscale = 1.5` on it. obj_growtangle_Create_0.gml:14-15 defaults maxxscale = maxyscale = 2, so the REGULAR turns get a NARROWED box: spr_battlebg_0 is 75x75 origin 37,37 (sprites.tsv:4100), so 1.5 x 2 = 112.5 wide by 150 tall, against the usual 150x150. Also carries scr_moveheart(), the floor `scr_turntimer(90)` and `global.mnfight = 2`. TWO TRAPS INSIDE. (a) HEALING-EGG TRAP: the growtangle create is the THIRD arm of an if/else-if chain whose first two arms test `global.monsterhp[...] < global.monstermaxhp[...] * 0.7` (Step_0:516-521). If the studio replays this with monsterhp unpopulated (0 or undefined), the chain takes arm 1, sets healing_egg_con = 1, and NEVER CREATES THE BOX OR THE SOUL. Seed global.monsterhp[i] = global.monstermaxhp[i] = 2060 for BOTH enemies first. (b) `if (powerup == 4)` at Step_0:526-530 (which would widen maxxscale to 2) is DEAD — see cut[].

boxBlockFinale._note: The two FINALE attacks (types 132 and 307) do NOT use boxBlock. They are set up inside `if (endcon == 2.5) { if (endtimer == 1) { ... } }`, and there is NO `maxxscale = 1.5` here — the finale box is the untouched obj_growtangle default 2 x 2 (150 x 150). Supplied as LITERAL SOURCE rather than as an anchor pair because there is no clean slice: `if (endtimer == 1)` occurs 5 times in the file (Step_0:775, 837, 1117, 1186, 1315) and `scr_turntimer(90);` occurs twice (535, 845), while slicing `if (endcon == 2.5)` with endAnchor `if (endtimer == 12)` produces a brace-UNBALANCED fragment (tested: 382 chars, one unmatched `{`). Both finale attacks then mutate the box themselves — type 132 lerps `obj_growtangle.image_xscale` to 3 over 30 frames (obj_attack_orange_superattack_Draw_0.gml:34-35), and type 307 swaps `obj_growtangle.sprite_index` AND `mask_index` to spr_battlebg_round (obj_omega_pan_manager_Create_0.gml:4-5), an 80x80 circle (sprites.tsv:326) — the box turns ROUND for the OMEGA PAN.

dispatchBlock._verified: Step_0:573-614, 1407 chars, brace-balanced, anchor occurs exactly once. No endAnchor — do NOT slice to `if (global.mnfight == 2 && global.turntimer <= 1 && endcon == 0)`, because Step_0:615 closes the enclosing bullets-phase if and the slice would carry a stray `}`.
dispatchBlock._note: The WHOLE per-turn dispatcher: it self-selects on obj_orange_enemy.uppercut_life and carries BOTH scr_turntimer calls (360 and 270). Replay this INSTEAD of manually spawning a controller, never in addition — that is the Knight double-spawn trap. Requires obj_orange_enemy to exist with `myself`, `mytarget` and `uppercut_life`, and healing_egg_con == 0 on self.

finaleDispatchBlock._verified: Step_0:849-879, 1026 chars, brace-balanced, anchor occurs exactly once.
finaleDispatchBlock._note: The finale dispatcher. Branches on the controller's own `condescendending` / `admireending` booleans, so the studio sets exactly ONE of them true on the controller instance to choose type 132 vs type 307. There is no controller-side flag like Jevil's joker = 1.

turnBlockNote: This fight has NO separate turn-length ladder, so there is no valid turnBlock and the field is deliberately null. Every scr_turntimer call except the floor is INSIDE a dispatcher branch, interleaved with the `instance_create(..., obj_dbulletcontroller)` calls (Step_0:595, 605, 861, 874), so no slice can set the turn length without also re-spawning a controller. The only standalone call is the base `scr_turntimer(90)` at Step_0:535, which already lives inside boxBlock and is the wrong value for all four attacks. (For the record: anchor `scr_turntimer(90);` + endAnchor `}` — the shape yellow_blue.json and watercooler.json use — would slice from Step_0:535 and additionally re-run `global.mnfight = 2; ballooncon = -1;`, for a turn length of 90 that is wrong every time.) Use `turnByType` below, or replay dispatchBlock / finaleDispatchBlock verbatim, which carry the right values themselves. Note scr_turntimer only RAISES (scr_turntimer.gml: `if (global.turntimer < arg0) global.turntimer = arg0;`) — but types 314 and 132 use a DIRECT `global.turntimer = N` assignment, which also lowers.

turnByType._note: 131 needs the EXTERNAL scr_turntimer(270) at Step_0:605 — obj_attack_green_cookingtime never sets global.turntimer, it only READS it (Draw_0:197-198 destroys itself at `global.turntimer < 1`). 314 is self-sufficient: obj_dbulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:3574 does a DIRECT `global.turntimer = 360;`, matching the dispatcher's scr_turntimer(360). 132 is self-sufficient and OVERRIDES the dispatcher: obj_dbulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:1626 does `global.turntimer = 615;` while Step_0:861 only asked for 300 — the real Orange finale is 615 frames, not 300. 307 needs the EXTERNAL scr_turntimer(500) at Step_0:874; obj_omega_pan_manager never touches global.turntimer. TYPE 131 IS FURTHER REWRITTEN MID-TURN by obj_orange_enemy_Step_0.gml:623-624 (`global.turntimer = 2`), :634 (`= 170`) and :816 (`= 30`) when the eat-and-power-up finale runs — see mechanics.

perTurn._note: The COMPLETE per-turn chooser: two arms, one input (obj_orange_enemy.uppercut_life), no numeric selector. When healing_egg_con != 0 the whole `if` is skipped and NO controller is created at all — that is the HEALING EGG turn replacement.

finale._note: `condescendending` is set (with endcon = 1) at Step_0:117-126 when `global.mercymod[obj_orange_enemy.myself] >= 100`; `admireending` at Step_0:128-137 when `global.mercymod[obj_green_enemy.myself] >= 100`. Orange is tested FIRST, so a simultaneous 100/100 gives the condescend ending. Step_0:706-763 is a SECOND `endcon = 1` trigger at the end of a bullet turn that sets NEITHER flag — see mechanics.

real.name: COOKING TIME — Green's FAST FOOD (falling food to catch + green flame bullets)
real.evidence: gml_Object_obj_orange_green_controller_Step_0.gml:597-606 — the `else` arm of the ONLY per-turn dispatcher, taken whenever obj_orange_enemy.uppercut_life >= 1 and healing_egg_con == 0. uppercut_life starts at 5 (obj_orange_enemy_Create_0.gml:15) and is reset to 5 after every type 314 (Step_0:592-593) and at both ending triggers (:122-123, :133-134), so type 131 is ALWAYS the first bullet turn of the fight and the default every turn after. obj_dbulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:1588-1598 hides obj_green_enemy and creates obj_attack_green_cookingtime. THAT OBJECT HAS NO STEP EVENT — its entire attack is in gml_Object_obj_attack_green_cookingtime_Draw_0.gml (198 lines). Shape: every `timermax` frames it drops one item at one of three landing spots (landingspot_x[0..2] = camerax()+272/306/336, or +283/318/352 when powerup == 2; Create_0:23-32). Every 3rd drop (`(mode2count % 3) == 0`, skipped entirely at powerup 5) is a HARMFUL obj_regularbullet with spr_bullet_green_flame, damage 96, target 4, gravity 0.35 (Draw_0:54-79). All other drops are obj_bullet_healing FOOD (Draw_0:123-191): foodtype 0 = spr_bullet_green_egg (gravity 0.35, then scr_doom(candy, 80)), foodtype 1 = spr_donut_bullet (vspeed -14 - random(6), bounces wall to wall), foodtype 2 = spr_swatchling_platter_candy (lerped to alternating box edges). Catching food heals ALL THREE heroes 1 HP and gives 4 TP each, and revives downed heroes to 1 HP (obj_bullet_healing_Step_0.gml:101-193 — scr_healall(1) + per-hero scr_tensionheal(4); candy adds scr_tensionheal(7), donut scr_tensionheal(4)). MISSING food lets Orange punch it — see mechanics. powerup drives cadence `timermax` 12/13/10/6/(8)/10 for 0/1/2/3/(4)/5 (Draw_0:7-27) and foodtype: 0 -> 0, 1 -> alternates 1/0, 2 -> 2, 3 -> 0, 5 -> alternates 1/0 (Draw_0:86-121). The controller also raises the soul's speed for this type: powerup >= 1 -> obj_heart.wspeed = 7, powerup >= 5 -> 10 (Step_0:24-52).

real.name: OMEGA-3 uppercut — Orange leaps the box and slams down expanding glove rings
real.evidence: gml_Object_obj_orange_green_controller_Step_0.gml:582-596 — the `if` arm, taken when obj_orange_enemy.uppercut_life < 1. uppercut_life starts at 5 and drops by 1 every time a food item falls past `obj_growtangle.y + 100` during a type-131 turn and Orange punches it (obj_orange_enemy_Step_0.gml:541-594, `uppercut_life--` at :553, clamped at -3 by :555-556). So this fires on the turn AFTER the player lets 5+ foods through, and Step_0:592-593 then resets uppercut_life to 5. Fully reachable and repeatable. obj_dbulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:3567-3712: the dispatcher PINS `difficulty = 8`, so the branch's own `if (difficulty == 0) difficulty = 9;` (:3571-3572) is dead for the real fight, and difficulty becomes obj_glove_manager.bullets (:3693-3694) — 8 gloves per ring. Every 56 frames Orange lerps to (growtangle.x +/- (56 + random(24)), growtangle.y - 144 + random(20)) trailing afterimages (:3592-3646), winds up at %56 == 15 (:3650), punches at %56 == 22 spawning a spr_orange_screenpunchfist obj_bulletparent flash (:3660), and at %56 == 25 drops an obj_glove_manager (:3691-3699) whose event_user(0) rings `bullets` obj_orange_glove around it (obj_glove_manager_Other_10.gml). The ring falls at `vspeed -> 0.7 + obj_heart.wspeed / 2`, its radius pulses `(90 + 33*sin(expand)) * grow` and each glove orbits at `turn / dist` (obj_glove_manager_Step_0.gml:1-33). At %56 == 30 the controller does `mytimer += 3 * (obj_heart.wspeed - 4)` (:3704-3705) — the faster the soul, the sooner the next punch. `gloveflip` alternates sides. `running` flips false once `global.turntimer < 64` (:3594-3595), which is how Orange retreats, so a wrong turn length breaks the retreat. Decompiler artifact at :3581: `orange = 402;` is the raw object id of obj_orange_enemy (objects.tsv line 404, header on line 1 -> id 402), then :3586 reads `bspr = orange.sprite_index;` object-scoped through that integer. Controller also sets soul speed: powerup >= 1 -> wspeed 5, >= 3 -> 6, >= 5 -> 7 (Step_0:54-82).

real.name: OMEGA-3 SUPER ATTACK — Orange's finale (condescend / Orange-mercy ending)
real.damageNote: The DISPATCHER SETS NO DAMAGE for this type. obj_attack_orange_superattack_Create_0.gml sets its own `damage = global.monsterat[obj_orange_enemy.myself] * 5` and `target = 4`; the debris then routes through the controller's event_user(1) instead (35/55/70).

real.name: OMEGA PAN — Green's finale: three orbiting pans firing flame fans (admire / Green-mercy ending)
real.evidence: gml_Object_obj_orange_green_controller_Step_0.gml:864-875, the same `if (endcon == 2.5) { if (endtimer == 12) }` block. Reached only when `admireending` is true, set at Step_0:128-137 when `global.mercymod[obj_green_enemy.myself] >= 100` (four FeastX acts). Note the dispatcher writes damage TWICE — `__dc.damage = global.monsterat[green] * 5;` at :870 then `__dc.damage = 92;` at :872 — and pins `__dc.target = 4` at :873. Fires exactly ONCE per fight. obj_dbulletcontroller_Step_0.gml:3455-3463 creates obj_omega_pan_manager at the box centre and scr_bullet_inherit()s it. Its Create_0 REPLACES `obj_growtangle.sprite_index` and `.mask_index` with spr_battlebg_round (80x80 circle) and spawns three obj_omega_pan at radius 140, 120 degrees apart, shuffled into a ds_list. Step_0 rotates them 0.5 deg/frame with a breathing radius (`120 + 6*cos(global.time * 0.25)`) and a swinging tangential offset (`-32 - 32*sin(global.time * 0.125)`), and every 35 frames the next pan in the shuffled list fires a 3-bullet fan of obj_omega_pan_fire (spr_bullet_green_flame, speed 9, gravity -0.3 along its own direction, middle bullet +2 speed). This is the only entry that takes the admire branch, and it is the only one followed by the `endcon == 3.1 -> 3.4` Susie/Ralsei praise scene (Step_0:908-912, 916-979).

real.name: HEALING EGG — turn REPLACEMENT: no controller, no bullets, no box, no soul
real.evidence: gml_Object_obj_orange_green_controller_Step_0.gml:516-519 sets healing_egg_con = 1 (Green heals itself) or 2 (Green heals Orange, only when Orange is the more wounded of the two) whenever an enemy is below 70% max HP, and every downstream guard then suppresses the entire bullet turn: :520 skips obj_growtangle, :532 skips scr_moveheart, :554 skips Orange's punch stance, :580 skips the dbulletcontroller entirely. Step_0:1609-1643 then prints `* GREEN cast HEALING EGG on self!` / `...on ORANGE!`, spawns obj_green_egg_heal with `target_enemy` set, pins `global.turntimer = 999` while the writer and the egg live, and drops it to -10 to end the turn; :1645-1653 clears the flag. FULLY REACHABLE AND REPEATABLE: both enemies clamp their own HP UP to 50% of max every single step (obj_orange_enemy_Step_0.gml:1-2 and obj_green_enemy_Step_0.gml:1-2), so any party that deals more than 30% damage crosses the 70% line, and obj_healing_egg_Draw_0.gml:48-58 restores the target to FULL max HP. Note the enemy-talk phase short-circuits for this too: Step_0:139-143 jumps straight to `global.mnfight = 1.5` with no dialogue when either enemy is under 70%. Listed as a real roster entry but not as an attack — like Pink's dates, it REPLACES a turn.

cut.name: powerup == 4 — the entire fifth difficulty tier
cut.evidence: The powerup ladder at gml_Object_obj_orange_green_controller_Step_0.gml:8-21 assigns 0, 1, 2, 3 and then JUMPS to 5: `if (_progress >= 80 && _progress < 100) powerup = 5;`. There is no arm that produces 4, and Create_0.gml:43 initialises it to 0. A chapter-wide grep for `powerup` shows the only writers are those six lines. So everything gated on `powerup == 4` is dead: the box widening `if (powerup == 4) with (obj_growtangle) maxxscale = 2;` (Step_0:526-530, sitting inside boxBlock), the Cooking Time cadence `timermax = 8` (obj_attack_green_cookingtime_Draw_0.gml:23-24) and the `foodtype = 2` platter-candy assignment (ibid:106-107). Separately, `if (powerup >= 4) wspeed = 6;` (Step_0:70-74) is not dead but is a NO-OP — `powerup >= 3` two lines above already set 6.

cut.name: Cooking Time `mode == 1` — the low-gravity food variant
cut.evidence: obj_attack_green_cookingtime_Create_0.gml:12 sets `mode = 2` and nothing anywhere ever reassigns it (grep over Ch5: that Create line is the only write to this object's `mode`). Draw_0:140-141, `if (powerup >= 1 && mode == 1) candy.gravity = choose(0.35, 0.35, 0.1);`, can therefore never run, so the healing food never gets the slow-float variant. Its sibling at Draw_0:74-75 tests `mode == 2` and DOES run, giving the green flame bullets `choose(0.35, 0.45, 0.25)` gravity at powerup >= 1.

cut.name: treasurehunter — the food-magnet modifier (plus five write-only Create vars)
cut.evidence: obj_bullet_healing_Step_0.gml:24-29 makes every food item home 6 px/frame toward the soul when `obj_orange_green_controller.treasurehunter` is true and the soul is within 30 px. obj_orange_green_controller_Create_0.gml:41 sets `treasurehunter = false;` and that is the ONLY assignment in Chapter 5, so the magnet never engages. Five more Create-only variables have neither a reader nor a second writer: `admirecount` (Create_0:37), `condescendcount` (:38), `heartspeed` (:42), `admiregreenonly` (:44), `condescendorangeonly` (:45). `afterbulletcon` (:17) is the mirror case — it HAS a reader (obj_battlecontroller_Step_0.gml:29 exits the whole battle step while it is > 0) but no writer anywhere, so that hook is dead too, as is its partner `afterbullettimer` (:18).

cut.name: obj_bullet_green_food / obj_omelet_cut — orphan bullet objects
cut.evidence: obj_bullet_green_food (objects.tsv:787, parent obj_collidebullet, sprite spr_bullet_green_egg, with Create/Step/Draw/Other_15) and obj_omelet_cut (objects.tsv:831, sprite spr_bullet_green_egg_half) have NO creator anywhere in Chapter 5 — `grep -rl` for each name across the whole dump returns ZERO files. The shipped fight uses obj_bullet_healing (no parent at all, objects.tsv:695) for food and obj_omelet_marker (objects.tsv:148, referenced only from obj_orange_green_controller_Step_0.gml and obj_orange_enemy_Step_0.gml) for the punched-food trophies. obj_bullet_green_food_Other_15.gml is a graze-style handler that never fires.

cut.name: the flagless second `endcon = 1` at Step_0:706
cut.evidence: gml_Object_obj_orange_green_controller_Step_0.gml:706-763 fires a SECOND `endcon = 1` at the end of a bullet turn when either mercy is >= 100, and it revives every downed hero to 5 HP — but it sets NEITHER condescendending NOR admireending. If that path were ever taken first, the whole finale would play with no message and no attack (the `if (endtimer == 12)` dispatcher at :854 and :864 would match neither branch). In practice it is unreachable as a first trigger: mercy can only change during the ACT phase, which precedes enemytalk, and the enemytalk check at :117-137 runs first and exits. Treat it as a safety net, not a fifth attack — but do not delete it, because it is what revives downed heroes before the finale.

exclusions.obj_enemy_orange_example: DEV TEMPLATE — confirmed excluded, not merely assumed. It is NEVER instantiated: a recursive grep over all of Chapter 5 for `obj_enemy_orange_example` finds hits only inside its own event files. It has no `scr_enemy_object_init()`, no obj_monsterparent lineage (objects.tsv:903 — the parent column is EMPTY, unlike obj_orange_enemy at :404 whose parent is obj_monsterparent), no entry in scr_encountersetup and no RoomCC. Its Create_0 makes its OWN battle box at hard-coded screen coordinates. Its 461-line Draw_0 is the visible ancestor of obj_attack_green_cookingtime / obj_attack_orange_superattack.
exclusions.obj_enemy_green_example: DEV TEMPLATE, same reasoning (objects.tsv:848, empty parent column). Never instantiated; the only references in the entire chapter are three lines in obj_enemy_orange_example_Draw_0.gml (:3, :44, :48) reaching across from its sibling template. Its Draw_0:68 reads `obj_orange_green_controller.powerup`, which is the one line that makes it LOOK connected — but nothing ever creates it, so that read never executes.
exclusions.obj_orangeheart_enemy: NOT PART OF THIS FIGHT — the starting lead was wrong. The whole obj_orangeheart_* family is the ORANGE SOUL platformer mode and belongs to FLOWERY; the shared colour word is a coincidence. obj_orangeheart_enemy (objects.tsv:778, parent obj_bulletparent) has exactly TWO references in Chapter 5, both in gml_Object_obj_debug_orangeheartcontroller_Step_0.gml:948-949, inside that object's `if (attacktype == 4)` branch — and NOTHING in the chapter ever sets `attacktype = 4` (grep over obj_dbulletcontroller_Step_0.gml shows attacktype written only as 0, 2 or 3), so even that one creator is itself dead. obj_orangeheart_enemy_Create_0.gml:14 sets `sprite_index = spr_flowery_walk_left_jacket_hand_up`. Neither obj_orange_enemy, obj_green_enemy nor obj_orange_green_controller mentions obj_orangeheart in any form.

mechanics:
STORY BATTLE, ONE ENCOUNTER, MERCY-ONLY, NO SOUL MODES. Launched exactly once, by `scr_battle(221, 3, orange_marker, green_marker, 0);` at gml_Object_obj_ch5_DWCR03_Step_0.gml:1055 (room_dw_fcastle_green_orange_battle). Encounter 221 (scr_encountersetup.gml:826-837) places obj_orange_enemy at xx+500/yy+103 as monstertype 113 and obj_green_enemy at xx+493/yy+180 as monstertype 114, battlemsg `* Green brings the food!&* Orange brings the fight!`. Both are 2060 HP / AT 16 / DF 0 / 0 EXP / 400 gold / sparepoint 0 / mercymax 100 (scr_monstersetup.gml:395-412 and :425-442). YOU CANNOT KILL THEM: the first two lines of BOTH enemy Steps clamp `global.monsterhp[myself]` back up to `maxhp * 0.5` every frame. The fight ends only when one of them reaches 100 mercy.

DISPATCH IS A TWO-LEVEL BOOLEAN, NOT A SELECTOR. The whole fight is four `instance_create(..., obj_dbulletcontroller)` calls in obj_orange_green_controller_Step_0.gml (584, 599, 856, 866). Per turn, at rtimer 12 of the bullets phase: `if (obj_orange_enemy.uppercut_life < 1) type 314 else type 131`, both suppressed when healing_egg_con != 0. Finale, at endcon 2.5 / endtimer 12: `if (condescendending) type 132` / `if (admireending) type 307`. There is no monsterattackname, no rr ladder, no myattackchoice. `rr` is a DECOY: Create_0:7 sets it to 0 and Step_0:647 does `rr = choose(0, 1, 2)` purely to pick one of three flavour battle messages.

THE CORE MINIGAME — OMELET CATCH. During every type-131 turn Green rains obj_bullet_healing food plus green flame bullets. Catching food with the soul heals all three heroes 1 HP and gives them 4 TP each, reviving downed heroes to 1 HP (obj_bullet_healing_Step_0.gml:101-193). Any food that falls past `obj_growtangle.y + 100` gets PUNCHED by Orange, who slides in from the box's left edge, plays spr_orange_punch_omelet, converts the food into an obj_omelet_marker trophy and decrements `uppercut_life` (obj_orange_enemy_Step_0.gml:541-594, clamped at -3). uppercut_life starts at 5. Once it hits 0 or below, that turn's Cooking Time ENDS EARLY and becomes a scripted eat-and-power-up sequence: obj_orange_enemy_Step_0.gml:623-624 forces `global.turntimer = 2` as soon as all bullets are gone, then :626-637 rewrites it to 170 and sets punchomeletcon = 2, which flies Orange to the box centre, quadruple-afterimages him, rockets him off the top of the screen (:751-756), drops him back on his start position with a screen shake and `global.turntimer = 30` (:794-817), then heals him `healamount` HP at turntimer 5 (:819-845) — healamount having been incremented once per omelet marker swallowed on the way up (:766). THE NEXT enemy turn is the type-314 uppercut, after which uppercut_life resets to 5. The HUD for all this is the 5-egg ring drawn around Orange (obj_orange_enemy_Draw_0.gml:96-155); at uppercut_life -1/-2/-3 it draws 6/7/8 eggs instead.

POWERUP — the difficulty axis, and a decompiler oddity that must be transpiled LITERALLY. obj_orange_green_controller_Step_0.gml:1-22 recomputes `powerup` from mercy every frame: 0-19 -> 0, 20-39 -> 1, 40-59 -> 2, 60-79 -> 3, 80-99 -> 5. The input at :3-6 reads `var _progress = global.mercymod[green]; if ((_progress == global.mercymod[green]) < global.mercymod[orange]) _progress = global.mercymod[orange];`. The inner comparison is ALWAYS TRUE (1), so the line reduces to `if (1 < mercymod[orange]) _progress = mercymod[orange];`. It is NOT a max(): it takes ORANGE's mercy whenever Orange has more than 1, and only falls back to Green's on the very first turn. Since every ACT gives Orange at least +20, powerup tracks Orange's mercy exclusively from turn 2 onward. "Fixing" this into a max() changes the fight. powerup drives Cooking Time's drop cadence and food type, and the soul's own walk speed (type 131: default 4 -> 7 at powerup >= 1 -> 10 at powerup >= 5; type 314: 5 / 6 / 7). At powerup 5 the `(mode2count % 3) == 0` flame-bullet branch is skipped entirely — the box becomes pure food, but the soul is moving at 10 px/frame. Because the ladder has no `100` arm and mercy clamps at 100, powerup HOLDS its last value at exactly 100 mercy.

HEROES SHAKE. obj_orange_green_controller_Step_0.gml:633-645 and :1588-1607: if the party catches ALL the food (uppercut_life unchanged across a turn) for 1/2/3 consecutive turns, `heroes_shake` becomes 1/2/3 and every obj_heroparent jitters +/-1, +/-2 or +/-3 px outside the bullets phase, with the battle message `* It's getting very hard to stay still!`. Cosmetic, but it is the only visible payoff for a perfect turn.

DIALOGUE STATE MACHINE. Two ladders, both keyed on whether Orange got his food: `orange_succeeded_getting_food_count` and `orange_failed_getting_food_count` step through half-integers 1 -> 1.5 -> 2 -> 2.5 -> 3 -> 3.5 -> 4 -> 4.5 (Step_0:145-308; note the branch at :148 tests `uppercut_life == uppercut_life_previous`, i.e. the player caught everything, and that is the FAILED ladder from Orange's point of view). These drive `ballooncon` chains 1-5 and 20-25 consumed in the `talked == 0.6` block (Step_0:358-495). It runs before every bullet turn and never changes WHICH attack fires.

THE TWO ENDINGS. Mercy comes only from the ACT menu: Orange's GetAlong (obj_orange_enemy_Step_0.gml:29-456, +25 orange / +20 green, four escalating Ralsei skits gated on `getalongcount`, force-jumped to skit 4 once `mercymod[orange] >= 75 || mercymod[green] >= 80` at :42-43) and Green's FeastX (obj_green_enemy_Step_0.gml:29-709, +25 green / +20 orange, four escalating dinner-table skits gated on `feastcount`, force-jumped at :47-48). Four GetAlongs -> orange 100 -> CONDESCEND ending -> type 132. Four FeastXs -> green 100 -> ADMIRE ending -> type 307 -> the unique `endcon == 3.1 -> 3.4` scene where Susie and Ralsei praise Green's attack and Orange sulks (Step_0:916-1000+). Orange is tested first (:117 before :128), so a simultaneous 100/100 gives the condescend ending. Powerup 5 is only seen on MIXED routes (e.g. 2 GetAlong + 2 FeastX puts both at 90 with neither at 100). After the finale attack the fight runs a long `endcon` cutscene (Step_0:771-1586) ending in obj_green_enemy sliding off screen and scr_wincombat(). obj_battlecontroller_Step_0.gml:17-26 freezes the whole battle step while `endcon > 0`.

SOUL: plain RED throughout. No green/purple/yellow/orange mode, no obj_purplecontrols, no soul-mode switch anywhere in the fight.

HAZARDS, roughly in the order they will bite:

1. DRAW-EVENT ATTACKS. obj_attack_green_cookingtime has NO Step event at all — its entire 198-line attack (timer, drop cadence, bullet creation, self-destruct) lives in Draw_0. obj_attack_orange_superattack's Step_0 is literally `exit;` and all 301 lines are in Draw_0. obj_green_egg_heal and obj_healing_egg are Create+Draw only. If the studio's loop skips Draw for invisible/off-screen objects, batches Draw at a different cadence than Step, or runs Draw zero times on the spawn frame, these attacks simply do not happen. The engine must run Draw exactly once per frame, in step order, for these objects.

2. THE HEALING-EGG BOX TRAP. boxBlock's growtangle create is the THIRD arm of an if/else-if chain whose first two arms test `global.monsterhp[...] < global.monstermaxhp[...] * 0.7`. Seed `global.monsterhp[i] = global.monstermaxhp[i] = 2060` for BOTH enemies (plus `global.monsterat[i] = 16`, `global.mercymod[i] = 0`, `global.monster[i] = 1`, and `myself` / `mytarget` on each enemy instance) before replaying anything, or neither the box nor the soul is ever created. The same 0.7 test at Step_0:139-143 short-circuits the enemy-talk phase.

3. DAMAGE IS ROUTED THROUGH THE CONTROLLER'S USER EVENTS. obj_orange_glove_Other_15.gml and obj_glove_manager_Other_15.gml both do `if (active == 1) with (obj_orange_green_controller) event_user(0);`; obj_omega_pan_fire_Other_15.gml and obj_bullet_orange_debris_Other_15.gml call `event_user(1)`. Other_10 (user 0) and Other_11 (user 1) then run `with (obj_orange_enemy) { ... }` and hit ALL THREE living heroes on ONE invulnerability window, for damage scaled by the party's collective HP fraction: gloves 46 / 70 / 90 (thresholds >= 0.5, >= 0.8), pan-fire and debris 35 / 55 / 70. Without those two events wired, every glove and every flame silently falls back to a single random hero at the bullet's own `global.monsterat * 5 = 80` — wrong number, wrong count. Both handlers need obj_orange_enemy to exist with writable `target`, `myself` and `remdamage`, and they clobber `global.inv` (set to -1 per hero, restored to `global.invc * 40`).

4. TURN LENGTH IS NOT SLICEABLE — see turnBlockNote / turnByType. 131 = 270 (external, and rewritten mid-turn to 2 / 170 / 30 by obj_orange_enemy_Step_0.gml:623-624, :634 and :816 when the eat sequence runs), 314 = 360 (self-set, and `running` flips false at `global.turntimer < 64`), 132 = 615 (self-set, OVERRIDES the dispatcher's 300), 307 = 500 (external). The studio's 90-frame floor is wrong for all four: at 90, Cooking Time terminates a third of the way in and Orange's uppercut loop retreats on its very first cycle.
